Section 1 of 17

Can You Really Become Free?

Some forms of bondage are easy to see.

A substance begins controlling someone’s choices. A relationship becomes abusive. Anger damages a family. Pornography reshapes the mind. Fear makes ordinary life feel unsafe.

Other struggles feel harder to explain.

A person may experience disturbing dreams, intense spiritual fear, pressure to return to forbidden practices, or a sense that something dark is trying to control their thoughts.

Whatever form bondage takes, it carries the same message:

“You will never be free.”

Jesus gives a different message.

Read John 8:34–36 ↗.

Jesus said that anyone controlled by sin is living in slavery. He also promised that when the Son sets someone free, that person is truly free.

Freedom does not come from pretending the struggle is small. It begins by bringing the truth into the light and placing your life under the authority of Jesus.

What Is Bondage?

Bondage is a pattern of control that keeps pulling someone away from the Creator’s will.

It may involve:

  • Alcohol or drugs
  • Pornography
  • Gambling
  • Sexual behavior
  • Anger and violence
  • Dishonesty
  • A controlling relationship
  • Fear of spiritual powers
  • Attempts to contact the dead
  • Divination or fortune-telling
  • Dependence on a spiritual object
  • A repeated destructive habit
  • Shame that keeps someone hiding
  • Hatred that will not release the past

Not every struggle has the same cause.

Some problems involve sinful choices. Some involve trauma, grief, physical illness, mental health, learned behavior, or chemical dependence. Some situations may include spiritual deception or harassment.

Several causes can be present at the same time.

Wisdom means taking the whole person seriously rather than forcing every struggle into one explanation.

Jesus Sees a Person, Not a Problem

Read Mark 5:1–20 ↗.

Jesus met a man whose life had been overtaken by evil spirits.

The man lived among tombs, separated from his community. He harmed himself, cried out, and could not be controlled by chains.

Other people saw someone dangerous and beyond help.

Jesus saw a human being who needed freedom.

The evil spirits recognized Jesus’ authority. Jesus commanded them to leave, and they obeyed.

Afterward, the man was sitting peacefully, clothed, and thinking clearly.

Jesus did not merely remove a spiritual power. He restored the man’s dignity, mind, relationships, and purpose.

No one is too broken, controlled, or spiritually trapped for Jesus to reach.

Jesus Has Complete Authority

Read Matthew 28:18 ↗.

Jesus has all authority in heaven and on Earth.

Read Colossians 2:14–15 ↗.

Through the cross, Jesus defeated the powers of darkness and exposed their weakness.

Satan still tempts and deceives, but he does not have unlimited power. Evil spirits must submit to the authority of Jesus.

Read Luke 4:33–36 ↗.

Jesus did not need complicated rituals, magic objects, or secret words. He spoke with authority, and the evil spirit obeyed.

Freedom comes through Jesus Himself.

Do You Need a Special Human Deliverer?

Jesus may work through trustworthy people who pray, teach Scripture, and offer wise support.

However, no human being owns the power of Jesus.

Be cautious if someone:

  • Claims that only they can free you
  • Demands large payments
  • Requires secrecy
  • Uses fear to create dependence
  • Touches you in a sexual or inappropriate way
  • Tells you to stop prescribed medication
  • Orders you to cut off every safe relationship
  • Claims that questioning them will bring a curse
  • Uses humiliation as part of deliverance
  • Makes dramatic claims that cannot be tested
  • Draws more attention to themselves than to Jesus

Read Acts 8:18–23 ↗.

The power of the Creator cannot be bought or sold.

A trustworthy helper points you toward Jesus, Scripture, prayer, truth, healthy support, and responsible care.

Can Someone Who Belongs to Jesus Still Be Attacked?

Read 1 Peter 5:8–9 ↗.

People who belong to Jesus can still experience temptation, accusation, fear, and spiritual opposition.

Jesus Himself was tempted by Satan.

Read Matthew 4:1–11 ↗.

Temptation does not mean Satan owns you. Spiritual pressure does not mean the Creator has abandoned you.

Read 1 John 4:4 ↗.

The Holy Spirit living within you is greater than the enemy.

A person who has surrendered to Jesus does not need to live as if evil spirits have the final claim over their life.

You may face a battle, but you do not have to surrender.

What Opens the Door to Bondage?

The Bible warns us against choices that place the mind under destructive influence.

Repeated sin

Read Romans 6:16 ↗.

Repeatedly surrendering to a behavior strengthens its control.

A choice becomes a pattern. A pattern becomes a habit. A habit can begin to feel like a master.

Spiritual practices outside the Creator’s direction

Read Deuteronomy 18:9–14 ↗.

Seeking guidance from spirits, mediums, divination, spells, fortune-telling, or the dead exposes a person to deception.

Curiosity does not make these practices safe.

Substances that weaken judgment

Read Proverbs 20:1 ↗ and 1 Peter 5:8 ↗.

The Creator calls us to remain alert and self-controlled.

Anything that repeatedly removes clear judgment can make harmful choices and spiritual deception easier.

Hidden shame

Read Proverbs 28:13 ↗.

What remains hidden often keeps its power.

Confession brings the struggle into the light, where forgiveness and healing can begin.

Hatred and unresolved anger

Read Ephesians 4:26–27 ↗.

Paul warned that anger can give the devil an opportunity.

This does not mean every person who struggles to forgive is controlled by a demon. It means hatred can become a place where the enemy continues feeding destructive thoughts.

Abusive control

Some bondage is created when another person uses threats, money, affection, violence, religion, or family pressure to control someone.

The Creator does not require you to remain under abuse.

Read Psalm 82:3–4 ↗.

Seeking safety and help can be an act of wisdom and truth.

Are You Guilty for What Your Ancestors Did?

No person inherits the spiritual guilt of an ancestor.

Read Ezekiel 18:19–20 ↗.

Each person is responsible for their own choices.

Family patterns can pass from one generation to another. Children may learn anger, addiction, fear, silence, or harmful ways of relating. The consequences of earlier choices may affect later generations.

But you are not automatically condemned because of something a relative practiced or believed.

Read 2 Corinthians 5:17 ↗.

When you belong to Jesus, your life receives a new spiritual foundation.

You do not need to reject your ancestry or renounce being Native. You need to surrender your own spiritual loyalties and choices to the Creator.

Jesus is stronger than every harmful pattern from the past.

Can Someone Place a Curse on You?

Words can cause real emotional and relational harm. Threats can create fear, and fear can shape behavior.

But no spoken curse is more powerful than the Creator.

Read Numbers 23:19–23 ↗.

No curse could stand against the people God had blessed.

Read Proverbs 26:2 ↗.

An undeserved curse has no place to settle.

If someone threatens to curse you:

  • Do not seek another spiritual practitioner to reverse it.
  • Do not answer one forbidden practice with another.
  • Bring your fear directly to Jesus.
  • Ask trusted followers of Jesus to pray with you.
  • Fill your mind with the Creator’s promises.
  • Refuse to organize your choices around fear.

Read Romans 8:31–39 ↗.

Nothing can separate those who belong to Jesus from the Creator’s love.

What Is the First Step Toward Freedom?

The first step is honesty.

Read Psalm 32:3–5 ↗.

David described the weight of hiding his sin. Relief began when he stopped concealing it and confessed to the Creator.

Tell God the truth about:

  • What you have practiced
  • What controls you
  • What you fear
  • What you want
  • What you regret
  • What you have hidden
  • Where you need help

The Creator already knows. Confession allows you to stop running and receive His forgiveness.

Read 1 John 1:9 ↗.

Jesus promises to forgive and cleanse those who confess.

What Does It Mean to Repent?

Repentance means turning away from one direction and moving toward the Creator.

Read Acts 3:19 ↗.

You may feel sorry and still return to the same practice. Repentance adds a decision and a change of direction.

If you want freedom from a spiritual practice, repentance means ending participation.

If you want freedom from addiction, repentance means accepting help and changing access, routines, and relationships connected with the addiction.

If you want freedom from anger, repentance means learning a different response and repairing harm.

Repentance becomes visible through action.

What Does It Mean to Renounce Something?

To renounce something means to reject its claim and withdraw your agreement.

You can say:

“Creator, I reject every spiritual practice, promise, invitation, or agreement that conflicts with Your Word. I choose Jesus as my only Savior and spiritual authority.”

You do not need to shout or repeat a formula until it feels powerful.

The strength is not in the wording. The strength is in Jesus and your sincere decision to belong to Him.

Read James 4:7–8 ↗.

Submit yourself to God. Resist the devil. Draw near to the Creator.

Submission comes before resistance.

Should You Remove Certain Objects?

Read Acts 19:18–20 ↗.

People who turned toward Jesus removed materials they had used for magic.

An ordinary object does not control a person by itself. The spiritual concern involves its purpose, use, and the loyalty connected with it.

If you personally own an object used specifically to contact spirits, practice divination, cast spells, seek supernatural protection, or gain spiritual power outside the Creator, remove it from that use.

Do not destroy cultural items simply because they look unfamiliar to you or to an outsider.

Regalia, artwork, jewelry, family belongings, photographs, language materials, and cultural symbols should not be labeled evil without understanding their actual meaning.

Ask:

  • What is this object?
  • What was it used for?
  • Is spiritual power believed to live within it?
  • Was it used to contact or honor a spirit?
  • Does keeping or using it draw me back toward a forbidden practice?
  • Can it be separated from that spiritual purpose?

If an item belongs to your family, nation, or community, do not destroy property that is not yours. Seek wise guidance about respectful and lawful handling.

The Creator calls you to reject spiritual allegiance to another power. He does not call you to destroy cultural identity.

What If the Bondage Is an Addiction?

Addiction can affect the mind, body, relationships, and spiritual life.

Someone may begin using a substance or behavior to cope with grief, loneliness, stress, trauma, or pain. What began as relief can become control.

Read 1 Corinthians 6:12 ↗.

Paul said he would not allow anything to master him.

Freedom may require:

  • Honest prayer
  • Medical care
  • Counseling
  • A recovery program
  • Support from trusted people
  • Removing access to the substance or behavior
  • Learning personal triggers
  • Changing routines
  • Addressing underlying pain
  • Restoring sleep and physical health
  • Daily accountability
  • Beginning again after a setback

Professional help does not compete with trust in the Creator. God can work through trained people and practical treatment.

Do not stop medication or medical treatment because someone claims your struggle is only spiritual. Discuss health decisions with a qualified medical professional.

What If You Keep Falling?

Read Proverbs 24:16 ↗.

A righteous person may fall and rise again.

Failure can teach you where your plan needs to become stronger.

After a setback, ask:

  • What was happening before I made the choice?
  • Was I tired, hungry, lonely, angry, stressed, or afraid?
  • What thought did I believe?
  • What access should I remove?
  • Who should I contact sooner next time?
  • What healthy action can replace the old response?

Do not let one failure become permission to continue.

Return to Jesus quickly. Confess, receive forgiveness, learn, and take the next faithful step.

Freedom often grows through many small decisions.

Replace the Old With Something New

Removing a harmful practice creates an empty space. That space must be filled.

Read Matthew 12:43–45 ↗.

Jesus warned about a person whose life was emptied but not filled with God’s presence. The former bondage returned with greater strength.

Lasting freedom requires more than stopping.

Fill your life with:

  • The Holy Spirit
  • Scripture
  • Prayer
  • Healthy relationships
  • Honest work
  • Rest
  • Service
  • Worship
  • Physical activity
  • Wise routines
  • Meaningful goals

Read Ephesians 4:22–32 ↗.

Paul repeatedly describes removing an old behavior and replacing it with a new one.

Stop lying and speak truth.

Stop stealing and begin working and giving.

Stop destructive speech and use words that build.

The Creator replaces bondage with a new way of living.

How Can Scripture Break Mental Bondage?

Read John 8:31–32 ↗.

Jesus said truth brings freedom.

Bondage often grows around a lie:

“I cannot live without this.”
“I will always be this way.”
“No one would love me if they knew.”
“My family’s past controls my future.”
“The Creator will never forgive me.”
“The spirit threatening me is stronger than Jesus.”

Read 2 Corinthians 10:4–5 ↗.

Bring destructive thoughts under the authority of Jesus.

Write down the lie. Then place a Bible promise beside it.

For example:

Lie: “I am permanently controlled.”

Truth: “If the Son makes you free, you shall be free indeed.” John 8:36 ↗

Lie: “The Creator abandoned me.”

Truth: “I will never leave you nor forsake you.” Hebrews 13:5 ↗

Lie: “My past defines me.”

Truth: “If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” 2 Corinthians 5:17 ↗

Lie: “The enemy is stronger.”

Truth: “He who is in you is greater than he who is in the world.” 1 John 4:4 ↗

Read these truths aloud when fear or temptation returns.

Why Does Community Matter?

Read Ecclesiastes 4:9–12 ↗.

Isolation strengthens many forms of bondage.

A person may hide because of shame, but secrecy removes support and accountability.

Choose safe people carefully.

A trustworthy support person:

  • Listens without humiliating you
  • Respects appropriate privacy
  • Takes danger seriously
  • Points you toward Jesus
  • Encourages professional help when needed
  • Does not try to control your choices
  • Tells the truth with compassion
  • Remains dependable over time

You do not need to tell everyone everything.

You do need someone safe enough to help you stop hiding.

What If Spiritual Fear Is Affecting Your Mental Health?

Some spiritual fears may have psychological, physical, or medical causes. Lack of sleep, trauma, medication reactions, substance use, anxiety, depression, and other health conditions can affect perception and thought.

If you are hearing voices, seeing things others do not see, losing sleep for long periods, feeling unable to control your actions, or thinking about harming yourself or someone else, seek professional help promptly.

You can pray while also speaking with a licensed mental health professional or medical provider.

Seeking care does not mean you lack faith.

The Creator cares about your mind, body, safety, and spiritual life.

A responsible spiritual helper will support appropriate care rather than demand that you choose between prayer and treatment.

How Should You Respond During Spiritual Fear?

If you believe you are experiencing spiritual harassment:

  1. Turn your attention toward Jesus.
  2. Pray simply and honestly.
  3. Refuse communication with the apparent spirit.
  4. Read a clear Bible promise.
  5. Ask trusted people to pray with you.
  6. Remove your involvement with forbidden practices.
  7. Care for sleep, sobriety, and physical health.
  8. Seek professional evaluation when symptoms may have a medical or psychological cause.
  9. Continue normal, healthy responsibilities when possible.
  10. Refuse to let fear become the center of your life.

You can pray:

“Jesus, I belong to You. Protect my mind and home. Remove every influence that does not come from You. Fill me with the Holy Spirit and give me peace.”

The prayer does not work as a magic formula. It expresses trust in the authority of Jesus.

What Does Lasting Freedom Look Like?

Freedom is more than one emotional moment.

Lasting freedom begins producing:

  • Clearer thinking
  • Greater self-control
  • Honest relationships
  • Willingness to receive help
  • Reduced secrecy
  • Stronger boundaries
  • Growing peace
  • Consistent prayer
  • Respect for Scripture
  • Freedom from spiritual fascination
  • Greater love for people
  • A life centered on Jesus

Some people experience immediate freedom. Others experience a longer process involving repeated prayer, treatment, accountability, and new habits.

Do not compare your timeline with someone else’s testimony.

The Creator knows how to lead you one step at a time.

Jesus Restores Purpose

After Jesus freed the man in Mark 5 ↗, the man wanted to leave with Him.

Read Mark 5:18–20 ↗.

Jesus told him to return home and tell his people what the Lord had done for him.

Jesus restored the man to his community and gave him a purpose.

He did not tell him to become ashamed of where he came from. He sent him back as a healed person who could bring hope to others.

Your struggle does not have to be the final chapter of your story.

The Creator can turn a place of bondage into a testimony of freedom. Your experience may one day help someone who believes freedom is impossible.

A Simple Plan for Beginning Freedom

Today

Tell the Creator the full truth.

Confess sin and ask for forgiveness.

Choose Jesus as your only spiritual authority.

Remove

End participation in practices that conflict with Scripture.

Reduce access to the substance, behavior, relationship, or setting connected with bondage.

Tell

Speak with one safe and trustworthy person.

Ask for prayer, accountability, and practical help.

Replace

Choose a Scripture, healthy routine, supportive relationship, and meaningful activity to fill the old space.

Continue

Expect growth to require daily choices.

If you fall, return to Jesus quickly.

Freedom is not proven by never facing another temptation. It is shown by learning to meet temptation with the power and truth of the Creator.

Think About It

Write your answers in your own words.

  1. What form of bondage feels most relevant to your life?
  2. Why is it important to understand the whole person rather than blame every struggle on a demon?
  3. What does the story in Mark 5 ↗ reveal about Jesus?
  4. What is the difference between guilt inherited from ancestors and patterns learned across generations?
  5. Is there a spiritual practice or unhealthy habit you need to renounce?
  6. Is there an object whose purpose or use you should examine?
  7. What lie helps keep the bondage in place?
  8. Which Bible promise answers that lie?
  9. Who is one safe person you can ask for help?
  10. What practical access, routine, or relationship needs to change?
  11. What would lasting freedom look like in your daily life?
  12. How could your future healing help someone else?

Try This During the Coming Week

Set aside fifteen quiet minutes each day.

Read one passage:

  • Day 1: Mark 5:1–20 ↗
  • Day 2: John 8:31–36 ↗
  • Day 3: Romans 6:6–18 ↗
  • Day 4: James 4:7–10 ↗
  • Day 5: Ephesians 4:22–32 ↗
  • Day 6: Ephesians 6:10–18 ↗
  • Day 7: Colossians 1:9–14 ↗

After each reading, write down:

  • What does this passage teach about bondage or freedom?
  • What does Jesus promise?
  • What lie do I need to reject?
  • What action should I take today?
  • Who can support that action?

Choose one clear step this week. Remove access to one harmful influence, contact one safe helper, attend one recovery meeting, schedule one professional appointment, or begin one healthy replacement habit.

A Prayer You Can Pray

Creator God, I bring You the truth about what has controlled, frightened, or harmed me. I confess every choice that has led me away from You. I reject every spiritual practice, promise, agreement, and source of guidance that conflicts with Your Word. Jesus, I choose You as my Savior and highest authority. Forgive me, cleanse me, and break the power of sin and darkness in my life. Fill me with the Holy Spirit. Replace lies with truth, fear with peace, secrecy with honesty, and bondage with freedom. Give me courage to accept help, wisdom to make practical changes, and strength to continue when the process is difficult. Use my restored life to bring hope to others. Amen.

Remember This

Jesus has complete authority over every power of darkness.

No one is too controlled, broken, or ashamed for Him to reach.

Not every struggle is caused by an evil spirit.

Physical, emotional, mental, relational, and spiritual needs should all be taken seriously.

You do not inherit spiritual guilt from your ancestors.

Following Jesus does not require rejecting your Native identity.

Repentance includes a real change of direction.

Renouncing evil means placing your spiritual loyalty completely with the Creator.

Cultural objects should not be condemned without understanding their meaning and use.

Addiction may require prayer, professional care, recovery support, and practical change.

Truth, community, healthy habits, and the Holy Spirit help freedom grow.

Your struggle does not have to become the final chapter of your story.
